좋다.e: 좋아요 = 'good!' or 'I like it'; 좋아하다 = to like.
좋다.t: Pronounced [조타]; the ㅎ is silent before a vowel: 좋아요 [조아요].

즐겁다.x: Traveling with my friends was really fun.
즐겁다.e: 즐거운 시간 보내세요 = 'Have a good time!'
즐겁다.t: 즐거운 주말 보내세요! = 'Have a nice weekend!'

무섭다.e: Means both 'scary' and 'scared'. 무서운 영화 = horror movie.
무섭다.t: The thing you fear takes 이/가: 저는 개가 무서워요 'I'm scared of dogs.'

포장.x: This store does gift wrapping for free.
포장.t: At a restaurant or café, 포장이요 means "To go, please"; eating in is 먹고 갈게요.

일정.ex: 이번 여행 일정이 너무 바빠서 좀 피곤해요.
일정.x: This trip's itinerary is so packed that I'm a bit tired.
일정.e: Literally 'day route' — the plan for each day.
일정.t: Pronounced [일쩡] — ㅈ after ㄹ becomes tense in Sino-Korean words.

기숙사.x: Most freshmen live in the school dorms.
기숙사.t: Pronounced [기숙싸] — the ㅅ becomes tense after ㄱ.

한복.x: Our whole family wore hanbok on Lunar New Year.
한복.t: Koreans often wear hanbok on holidays like 설날 and 추석, and at weddings.

움직이다.x: I'm going to take the picture, so don't move.
움직이다.e: The noun 움직임 'movement' comes from 움직이- + -ㅁ.
움직이다.t: Moving house is 이사하다, not 움직이다.

아깝다.m: to be a waste, to be a shame; to be too good to lose
아깝다.x: It felt like a waste to throw the food away, so I ate it all.
아깝다.e: Related to 아끼다 (to save, to cherish) — losing what you'd rather keep.

심장.x: I was so nervous that my heart was racing.

적극적.ex: 그 학생은 수업에 아주 적극적으로 참여해요.
적극적.x: That student participates very actively in class.
적극적.e: Literally 'piling up to the extreme'. -적 = '-ic/-ive': 긍정적, 부정적.
적극적.t: Pronounced [적끅쩍]; use 적극적인 before nouns and 적극적으로 as an adverb.

짜증 나다.forms: 짜증 나요 · 짜증 났어요 · 짜증 날 거예요 · 짜증 나는 (+noun)
짜증 나다.m: to be annoyed, irritated; to be annoying
짜증 나다.ex: 버스가 계속 안 와서 너무 짜증 나요.
짜증 나다.x: I'm so annoyed because the bus just won't come.
짜증 나다.e: 짜증 'irritation' + 나다 'to arise': irritation wells up.
짜증 나다.t: 짜증 나다 is feeling annoyed; 짜증을 내다 is showing it by snapping at someone.

실망.x: I was very disappointed when I saw my test results.

소독.x: You have to disinfect a wound first.
소독.t: Pronounced [소독] but 소독약 becomes [소동냑] through ㄴ-insertion and nasalization.

이용자.ex: 이 앱은 이용자가 천만 명이 넘어요.
이용자.x: This app has over ten million users.
이용자.e: 이용 'use' + -자 'person who does it': 운전자, 소비자.

조상.ex: 추석에는 가족이 모여서 조상께 차례를 지내요.
조상.x: On Chuseok, families gather and hold a memorial rite for their ancestors.

요청.x: I requested a week of vacation from my company.

포장마차.x: After work, I had some soju at a street tent bar.
포장마차.e: Literally 'cloth-covered horse cart': a tented stall selling snacks and drinks.
포장마차.t: Often shortened to 포차. Many indoor bars also use 포차 in their names.

팬 미팅.ex: 다음 달에 첫 팬 미팅이 열린대요.
팬 미팅.x: I heard their first fan meeting is being held next month.
팬 미팅.e: From English 'fan' + 'meeting'. Konglish: an event where stars talk, play games and perform for fans.
팬 미팅.t: Often written without a space: 팬미팅.

조직.ex: 우리 회사는 조직이 크지 않아서 분위기가 좋아요.
조직.x: Our company isn't a big organization, so the atmosphere is nice.
조직.e: Literally 'braid and weave' — people woven together into one structure.

호황.x: Back then the economy was booming, so there were lots of jobs.

인용.ex: 보고서에 다른 사람의 글을 인용할 때는 출처를 써야 해요.
인용.x: When you quote others' writing in a report, you must cite the source.
인용.t: Pronounced [이뇽]: the ㄴ moves over to the next syllable.

벼락치기.x: I crammed for the exam the night before.
벼락치기.e: From 벼락 'lightning' + 치다 'to strike': studying at lightning speed.
벼락치기.t: Common patterns are 벼락치기하다 and 벼락치기로 공부하다.

커닝.ex: 시험 중에 커닝을 하다가 선생님께 걸렸어요.
커닝.x: I got caught by the teacher while cheating on the test.
커닝.e: From English 'cunning' — but in Korean it means cheating on an exam.
커닝.t: Don't use 'cunning' in English for this; Americans say 'cheating'.

번역가.ex: 그 소설은 유명한 번역가가 영어로 번역했어요.
번역가.x: A famous translator translated that novel into English.
번역가.t: 번역가 translates written text; someone who interprets speech aloud is a 통역사.

인격.m: character, personality; dignity as a person
인격.x: You should respect other people's dignity.
인격.e: Literally 'a person's standing' — your worth as a human being.
인격.t: 인격 means moral character or dignity; for 'outgoing personality' use 성격 instead.

다정다감하다.x: My boyfriend has a warm, affectionate personality.

허영심.ex: 비싼 가방을 사는 것은 허영심 때문일 수도 있어요.
허영심.x: Buying an expensive bag might be because of vanity.

시급하다.x: Environmental problems must be solved urgently.
시급하다.t: Pronounced [시그파다]; don't confuse with 시급 'hourly wage' — 최저 시급.

스케일링.ex: 일 년에 한 번은 치과에서 스케일링을 받아요.
스케일링.x: I get my teeth cleaned at the dentist once a year.
스케일링.e: From English 'scaling' (removing tartar); in Korean it is the everyday word for a dental cleaning.
스케일링.t: Use 스케일링을 받다 'to get a cleaning'. National health insurance covers one scaling a year for adults, so it is cheap.

가성비.ex: 이 식당은 양도 많고 가성비가 좋아요.
가성비.x: This restaurant gives big portions and is good value for money.
가성비.e: Short for 가격 대비 성능 'performance relative to price': 가 'price' + 성 'performance' + 비 'ratio'.
가성비.t: Very common: 가성비가 좋다 'good value'; 가성비 갑 is slang for 'best value'.

환급.x: I got a tax refund after the year-end tax settlement.
환급.t: 환급 is for taxes and fees; for store purchases, use 환불.

관성.ex: 버스가 갑자기 서면 관성 때문에 몸이 앞으로 쏠려요.
관성.x: When the bus stops suddenly, your body lurches forward because of inertia.
관성.e: Literally 'habitual nature': things keep doing what they were doing.

수습하다.m: to bring under control, to handle (a situation); to recover (remains)
수습하다.ex: 정부는 사태를 수습하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
수습하다.x: The government is working to get the situation under control.
수습하다.e: Literally 'gather and pick up' — cleaning up a mess.
수습하다.t: A homonym 수습 (different hanja) means 'apprenticeship': 수습 기간 is a probation period.

몰락하다.m: to fall, to collapse, to be ruined
몰락하다.ex: 한때 잘나가던 그 기업은 무리한 투자로 몰락했어요.
몰락하다.x: That once-thriving company was ruined by reckless investment.

민법.ex: 결혼과 상속 문제는 민법에 따라 처리됩니다.
민법.x: Marriage and inheritance matters are handled under civil law.
민법.e: Literally 'people's law' — rules between private individuals.

수색.m: search (for a person or evidence), search operation
수색.x: The rescue team kept searching for the missing person all night.

발행인.ex: 신문 발행인은 기사 내용에 책임을 져야 해요.
발행인.x: A newspaper's publisher must take responsibility for its articles.

블랙홀.x: Scientists photographed a black hole for the first time.
블랙홀.t: Used figuratively too: 소비의 블랙홀 'a black hole of spending'.

모독하다.m: to insult, to defame, to profane
모독하다.x: His remarks were an insult to the victims.

야합하다.m: to make an illicit deal, to collude (in an unprincipled alliance)
야합하다.ex: 두 정당이 선거를 앞두고 야합했다는 비판을 받았습니다.
야합하다.x: The two parties were criticized for striking an unprincipled deal before the election.
야합하다.e: Literally 'joining in the wild' — an improper, unprincipled union.

주축.ex: 젊은 선수들이 팀의 주축을 이루고 있어요.
주축.x: Young players form the core of the team.

원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다.forms: 원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다더니 · 원숭이도 나무에서 떨어질 때가 있잖아요
원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다.m: even experts make mistakes, anyone can slip up (lit. even monkeys fall from trees)
원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다.ex: 원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다더니, 요리사인 형이 고기를 다 태웠어요.
원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다.x: They say even monkeys fall from trees — my brother, a chef, burned all the meat.
원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다.e: Literally 'even a monkey falls from a tree': the best climber can still slip.
원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다.t: Close to English 'Even Homer nods.' Used to tease or comfort a skilled person who has made a mistake.

모병제.ex: 모병제로 바꾸자는 주장이 다시 나오고 있어요.
모병제.x: Arguments for switching to a volunteer military are coming up again.
모병제.e: Literally 'system of recruiting soldiers' (as opposed to drafting them).
모병제.t: South Korea currently uses 징병제 (conscription); 모병제 is the frequently debated alternative.

결정론.ex: 결정론이 옳다면 우리의 선택도 이미 정해져 있는 셈이에요.
결정론.x: If determinism is right, then our choices are, in effect, already decided.
결정론.e: Literally 'decided theory': everything is fixed in advance.
결정론.t: Pronounced [결쩡논]: tensing after ㄹ, then ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

자책감.ex: 그는 사고가 자기 탓이라는 자책감에 시달렸어요.
자책감.x: He was tormented by guilt, believing the accident was his fault.

동맥경화.ex: 흡연은 동맥경화의 주요 원인 중 하나입니다.
동맥경화.x: Smoking is one of the main causes of hardening of the arteries.
동맥경화.e: Literally 'arteries becoming hard'; -화 = becoming: 노화, 경화.

가설검증.ex: 이 연구의 가장 중요한 목적은 바로 가설검증입니다.
가설검증.x: The most important purpose of this study is hypothesis testing.
가설검증.e: Literally 'examining and proving a tentative theory'.
가설검증.t: Often written with a space, 가설 검증, and used with 하다: 가설을 검증하다.

중공업.ex: 울산은 조선과 자동차 같은 중공업이 발달한 도시예요.
중공업.x: Ulsan is a city with developed heavy industries like shipbuilding and cars.
중공업.e: Literally 'heavy industry'; the opposite is 경공업.

지속하다.m: to continue, to sustain, to last
지속하다.ex: 정부는 경기 부양 정책을 당분간 지속하기로 했습니다.
지속하다.x: The government decided to continue its economic stimulus policy for the time being.
지속하다.e: Literally 'hold and continue' — keeping something going over time.
지속하다.t: In everyday writing 지속되다 is more common for situations; 지속 가능한 발전 means 'sustainable development'.

혼용하다.m: to use together, to mix (in use)
혼용하다.x: Old newspapers used Hangul and Chinese characters together.
혼용하다.e: Literally 'mix in use' — using two things side by side.
혼용하다.t: Pronounced [호뇽하다] — ㄴ links to the next vowel.

가뭇없다.m: vanished without a trace, completely gone
가뭇없다.ex: 그 많던 돈이 어느새 가뭇없이 사라졌어요.
가뭇없다.x: All that money has vanished without a trace.
가뭇없다.t: Pronounced [가무덥따]; mostly used as the adverb 가뭇없이 사라지다.

물질만능주의.m: materialism, the belief that money can do anything
물질만능주의.ex: 물질만능주의가 여러 사회 문제를 낳고 있다는 비판이 많아요.
물질만능주의.x: Many criticize materialism for causing various social problems.
물질만능주의.e: Literally 'the doctrine that material things can do everything'.
물질만능주의.t: Pronounced [물찔만능주의]: ㄹ followed by ㅈ in Sino words is tensed.

목불식정.m: completely illiterate, unable to read even the simplest letter
목불식정.ex: 그 시절에는 목불식정인 사람이 적지 않았어요.
목불식정.x: In those days, quite a few people couldn't read a single letter.
목불식정.e: Unable to recognize even the simplest character, one with just two strokes.
목불식정.t: The native saying 낫 놓고 기역 자도 모른다 has the same meaning.
